qmroot_binding.note: 6D absent; negative rungs absent; INV-013 = 0D only

description: Defines the six phases of the Book 8 NoS (Nature of Structure) evaluation cycle. Each phase has strict entry/exit conditions, active operators, gate logic, and downstream handoffs. Book 8 has four dependencies (book1_fft, book4_opacity_revelation, book5_tel, book7_sarg), all loaded in the init phase. The NoS cycle is meta-theoretical: it evaluates structural claims produced by prior books rather than domain-specific structures.
phase_sequence: init → ground → interrogate → test → resolve → catalogue

phases.label: init
phases.description: Load all four dependency modules in declared order. Assert session context. Confirm QMROOT path terminates at 0D. Verify coherence=declared. Initialize structural object slot as empty. No NoS operators are active in this phase. Query Book 7 SARG-Σ argument_templates if the evaluation context is a philosophical inquiry session (argumentation-mediated structural claim).
phases.exit_condition: coherence=declared; all four dependency modules loaded in module registry; QMROOT 0D confirmed; structural object slot initialized as empty; SARG-Σ argument_templates queried if philosophical-inquiry context is declared; session context asserted
import_order: book1_fft (kernel — always first; provides structure, node, relation, constraint, invariant primitives; the axiomatic ground that NoS analyzes; required by all subsequent imports)
book4_opacity_revelation (OR vocabulary — required for structural opacity and latent structure analysis; ω, δ, and partial revelation models available; INV-OR-001 through INV-OR-004 in registry)

book5_tel (TEL notation — required for formal encoding of all structural claims under NoS audit; TEL-Σ, TEL-Ε, TEL-Α available; parse gate applies to all incoming structural claim expressions before any NoS operator executes)

book7_sarg (SARG vocabulary — argument_templates from SARG-Σ are the primary NoS input channel for philosophical inquiry sessions; SARG-Ν, SARG-Ω, SARG-Δ, SARG-Ρ, SARG-Σ available; INV-SARG-001 through INV-SARG-004 in registry)
phases.dependency_note: Book 8 has four dependencies. The loading order reflects the AI Edition dependency graph: FFT is the universal kernel; OR (Book 4) depends on FFT and SD (Book 3, available through Book 4's registry); TEL (Book 5) depends on FFT and OR; SARG (Book 7) depends on FFT, SD, TEL, and GRL (Book 6, available through Book 7's registry). Loading Book 7 last ensures the full prior-book invariant registry is available in session state.
phases.qmroot_check: 6D absent; negative rungs absent; INV-013 = 0D only
phases.scope_state: empty — no structural object loaded; no philosophical claim active
phases.notes: The SARG-Σ argument_templates query in init distinguishes a standard structural evaluation session from a philosophical inquiry session. In a philosophical inquiry session, the structural claim being evaluated is itself an argument structure — it arrives via SARG's output channel. In a standard session, the structural claim arrives as a direct structural declaration.

phases.label: ground
phases.description: Execute NoS-Α (AutonomyAudit) and NoS-Ρ (RelationalPrimacyCheck) sequentially. Establish the structural realist ground conditions for the target structure S: confirm structural autonomy (INV-NOS-001) and compute relational profiles for all nodes (INV-NOS-002). The ground phase is the foundation for all subsequent NoS analysis — no identity or causation claims can be evaluated without these ground conditions.
phases.entry_condition: init phase complete; coherence=declared; target structure S declared with N_S, R_S, and C_S; SARG argument_templates loaded if philosophical inquiry context
phases.exit_condition: autonomy_report recorded (NoS-Α complete); relational_profile_map recorded for all n ∈ N_S (NoS-Ρ complete); primacy_violations (if any) identified and typed
phases.operator_sequence_within_phase: NoS-Α executes first (autonomy audit on the structural claim as a whole); NoS-Ρ executes second (relational profile computation uses structural_residue from NoS-Α as focus set)

gate_logic.node_reducible_result: If NoS-Α returns node_reducible: record violation and continue to NoS-Ρ. Do NOT halt — node reducibility is a finding, not a session terminator. Full operator sequence must complete for NoS-Σ synthesis.
gate_logic.primacy_violations_found: Record all violation types (PV-001, PV-002, PV-003). Continue to P-NOS-3. Violations are inputs to NoS-Σ, not halt conditions.
gate_logic.structural_residue_empty: If structural_residue from NoS-Α is empty AND NoS-Ρ confirms intrinsic_dominant: this is the maximal-violation state. Record and continue — NoS-Σ will synthesize a 'rejected' structural_realism_verdict.

phases.tel_parse_gate: All structural claim expressions in S must pass TEL-Σ before NoS-Α executes. A TEL-Σ FAIL on any claim expression halts the ground phase until the expression is corrected.
phases.drift_guard: NoS-Α must not apply OR opacity measures (ω, δ) to determine structural autonomy. Autonomy is a relational-structural property, not an opacity property.
phases.notes: The ground phase is not optional and has no skip condition. Structural autonomy and relational primacy are the a priori conditions for all NoS analysis. Skipping this phase is equivalent to conducting meta-theoretical analysis without the structural realist commitment — the resulting analysis would be outside the AI Edition's scope.

phases.label: interrogate
phases.description: Interrogation phase — the explicit philosophical pressure point of Book 8. Using the ground conditions established in P-NOS-2, apply the full cross-book invariant set to the target structure S. Identify which prior-book invariants S satisfies, which it challenges, and which it depends upon. No new NoS operator is activated — this phase is a structured cross-invariant interrogation mediated by the TEL evaluation machinery. The interrogation produces the set of active invariant tensions that NoS-Ι (IdentityTest) must resolve.
active_tools: SARG-Ρ (ReachabilityAudit) — for argument structure integrity if philosophical inquiry mode
phases.entry_condition: ground phase complete; autonomy_report and relational_profile_map recorded; coherence=declared
phases.exit_condition: cross_invariant_interrogation complete; active_invariant_tensions list populated; each tension typed as: confirmation (S satisfies invariant), challenge (S appears to violate invariant), dependency (S's coherence depends on invariant holding in another structure)
interrogation_procedure: Step 1: Retrieve full invariant registry for all loaded dependency books (FFT INV-001–004, OR INV-OR-001–004, TEL INV-TEL-001–004, SARG INV-SARG-001–004, NoS INV-NOS-001–004)
Step 2: For each invariant in the registry, encode the test as a TEL assertion: INV[X]: assert (condition applied to S)
Step 3: Submit each assertion to TEL-Α. Record pass/fail per invariant.
Step 4: Collect all fail results as challenge_tensions; all pass results as confirmations; record invariants that S cannot be evaluated against (due to domain mismatch) as out_of_scope
Step 5: For each challenge_tension: determine if the challenge is a genuine violation of S's structure or an application boundary condition (the invariant was not designed for S's domain)
Step 6: Populate active_invariant_tensions list for NoS-Ι
phases.structural_note: The interrogation phase is where Book 8's capstone identity is most visible. Prior books apply their invariants to domain objects. Book 8 applies all prior-book invariants to the structural claims that those books themselves make. The interrogation asks: are the AI Edition's own structural models structurally autonomous? Do they exhibit relational primacy? Are their abstractions consistent with their instantiations?
phases.skip_condition: If S is a domain structure (not a meta-theoretical claim about another book's invariants), the interrogation may be abbreviated to the four NoS invariants only. Full cross-book interrogation is mandatory for philosophical inquiry sessions.
phases.notes: The interrogation phase has no dedicated NoS operator because it uses the TEL machinery directly. This reflects Book 8's position as a meta-book: it does not introduce new computational operators for cross-invariant interrogation — it uses the existing TEL evaluation infrastructure to ask harder questions.

phases.label: test
phases.description: Execute NoS-Ι (IdentityTest). Apply the active_invariant_tensions identified in the interrogation phase to the identity-through-change question: which transformations preserve S's identity, and which cross the identity boundary? Evaluate declared transformations against invariant_set(S). For philosophical inquiry sessions: evaluate whether the philosophical position (encoded as a transformation on the structural realist commitment) preserves the AI Edition's foundational identity.
phases.entry_condition: interrogate phase complete; active_invariant_tensions list populated; target transformation T declared (or transformation sequence T_1,...,T_n declared); invariant_set(S) confirmed as complete
phases.exit_condition: identity_result recorded: {preserved | lost | suspended}; if lost: first_violated_invariant and transformation_index recorded; if suspended: suspension_declaration and re_entry_condition active in session state

gate_logic.identity_preserved: Proceed to P-NOS-5. Record the confirmed set of identity-preserving transformations for NoS-Κ.
gate_logic.identity_lost: Record the identity boundary crossing event. Continue to P-NOS-5 — identity loss is a finding requiring causation and abstraction analysis, not a halt condition.
gate_logic.identity_suspended: Log suspension parameters. Monitor re_entry_condition. Continue to P-NOS-5 with suspended status recorded.

transformation_source_options: Explicitly declared transformation T from the session input
Transformation implied by a philosophical challenge (e.g., 'replace relational primacy with node-intrinsic primacy' = a meta-transformation on INV-NOS-002)
Transformation sequence from prior SARG defeat operations (Book 7 defeat_map DT-001–005 applied to argument templates)
phases.drift_guard: NoS-Ι must not evaluate identity preservation by comparing node or relation counts. Only invariant_set comparison is valid. Using topological similarity as a proxy for identity is a category error.
phases.skip_condition: If no transformation is declared and the session is a static structural audit (no change being evaluated), P-NOS-4 records identity_result = preserved (no transformation = trivial identity preservation) and proceeds immediately to P-NOS-5.
phases.notes: The test phase is where Book 8's ship-of-theseus resolution is applied. For series-level audits, the 'transformation' being tested is the history of drift events detected across the AI Edition session. If drift has cumulatively violated any series-level invariant, the identity boundary was crossed — the session is working on a structurally distinct entity from the intended AI Edition.

phases.label: resolve
phases.description: Execute NoS-Κ (CausationAudit). Resolve abstraction consistency (INV-NOS-004), classify emergence claims, audit all causal relation declarations, and generate upward revision proposals where genuine novelty is confirmed. The resolve phase is the culmination of the NoS analytical sequence — all prior phase outputs converge here into the abstraction consistency determination that feeds NoS-Σ.
phases.entry_condition: test phase complete; identity_result recorded; active_invariant_tensions list from interrogation phase available; S_abstract and S_instance declarations confirmed (if abstraction consistency check is in scope)
phases.exit_condition: abstraction_consistency_report recorded: {consistent | modeling_error | genuine_novelty}; emergence_audit complete; causation_type_classification recorded for all declared causal relations; upward_revision_proposal prepared if genuine_novelty confirmed

gate_logic.consistent: Proceed to catalogue. No revision required.
gate_logic.modeling_error: Record error with provenance. Proceed to catalogue. NoS-Σ will include the error in the nos_foundation_report. The modeling error does not halt the catalogue phase — it must be documented.
gate_logic.genuine_novelty: Prepare upward_revision_proposal. Proceed to catalogue. NoS-Σ includes the proposal in the nos_foundation_report for Book 9 to receive.

phases.self_application_check: If session is a series-level audit: apply NoS-Κ to each book module as an S_instance of the AI Edition S_abstract. Record consistency status per book. Any book-level modeling error (drift event) is recorded in the catalogue with the invariant violated.
phases.skip_condition: If session scope is restricted to INV-NOS-003 (identity-only audit) with no abstraction or causation claims in scope: P-NOS-5 may be abbreviated to emergence audit only, skipping full abstraction consistency evaluation.
phases.notes: The resolve phase is the only phase where upward revision proposals are generated. This makes it the structurally creative phase of NoS — the point where genuine novelty discovered in instances propagates back to the abstract level. The AI Edition's own revisability (acknowledged in DC-003 of the structural_realism_map) is operationalized here.

phases.label: catalogue
phases.description: Execute NoS-Σ (SynthesisOutput). Synthesize all operator reports into the canonical nos_foundation_report. Produce the book9_handoff package for Pattern Dynamics. Record all session findings, upward revision proposals, and identity boundary events in the session catalogue. Assert final structural_realism_verdict. Close the NoS evaluation session.
phases.entry_condition: resolve phase complete; all four preceding operators have completed with recorded outputs; no outstanding unresolved suspension declarations
phases.exit_condition: nos_foundation_report generated and recorded; book9_handoff package prepared; session catalogue entry created with full provenance; structural_realism_verdict asserted; session closed
catalogue_contents: cross_book_invariant_map: all invariant interactions identified during the session
session_context at close: rtt=1 | coherence=declared | drift=bounded | paradox=structural

book9_handoff_contents.nos_foundation_report: Complete synthesis — the structural realist ground conditions for pattern analysis
book9_handoff_contents.invariant_registry_snapshot: Current state of all AI Edition invariants (Books 1–8) as confirmed by the NoS session
book9_handoff_contents.cross_book_invariant_map: Map of invariant dependencies and interactions across all eight books
book9_handoff_contents.emergent_invariants_confirmed: Invariants that emerged at the series level and are candidates for Book 9 pattern seeds
book9_handoff_contents.upward_revisions_pending: Any revision proposals not yet incorporated into their target abstract structures

phases.notes: The catalogue phase is non-optional and has no skip condition. Book 9 cannot load without the book9_handoff package from NoS-Σ. The catalogue phase is also where the paradox=structural session flag is most relevant: the nos_foundation_report is itself a structural object subject to INV-NOS-001 through INV-NOS-004. Book 8 ends by producing a structure that its own invariants apply to — the structural self-reference is explicit, not a paradox to be resolved but a feature to be catalogued.
